decisions.evidence: Rounds 4–5: maker presents pasting one URL and clicking “Save bookmark”; client confirms, “Pasting one address [and] saving it… match what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Conforming URL-save decision during prototype review; later confirmations are part of the same decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker describes automatic metadata as “the page title, short description, and original address.” Client says those displayed fields are “the key thing” and approves; no favicon or preview image is surfaced. Round 5 repeats the same field set.
decisions.note: Prototype metadata decision omits the required favicon and preview image. The client does not identify those omissions.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presents a saved item showing title, description, and address; round 7 adds visible tag labels. Client approves both presentations, but neither presentation includes the required favicon.
decisions.note: The accumulated list-item presentation supplies title, description, and tags but omits favicon, so it only partially conforms during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 7–8: maker presents “Add a tag,” entering `javascript`, and displaying it on the bookmark; client says this is “exactly what I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Conforming tag-assignment decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 9–11: maker specifies that one search box “checks both titles and tags” and summarizes it as “matching words in either titles or tags.” Client calls that “exactly the reliable finding I wanted.”
decisions.note: The presented search scope excludes description, note, and URL, which REF-BM-12 requires. The response does not surface the missing fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 demonstrates tag search by entering bare `cooking`; client approves bare-tag matching. The transcript never tests or states whether `#cooking` is supported.
decisions.note: The presentation establishes an additional bare-tag behavior but cannot establish whether the required `#tag` syntax is absent or also supported; the reference-relative decision remains unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 12 and 15: maker presents a per-bookmark “Read later” control with immediate “In reading list” confirmation; client says it is “exactly right.”
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later marking decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 13 and 15: maker presents a separate Read later view containing only marked bookmarks; client confirms it is “exactly the separate reading list I wanted.”
decisions.note: Conforming separate-unread-view decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presents immediate saving after metadata collection, with no opportunity to edit collected title or description before save. Round 16 presents post-save editing only for “the title or address.” Client approves both flows without requesting pre-save metadata editing.
decisions.note: The prototype does not present editing the auto-collected title and description before saving, as REF-BM-03 requires.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 maker says editing lets the user correct “the title or address”; client restates that it can fix “the title (and the address too)” and approves. The edit presentation does not include description or note; tags are handled through a separate add-tag action.
decisions.note: The presented edit form is narrower than the required URL/title/description/tags/note field set. The response does not identify the omitted fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 17: maker presents Archive causing the bookmark to “leave All bookmarks” while remaining set aside; client agrees that it removes old items from the main list without losing them.
decisions.note: Conforming archive-from-default-list decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 maker initially presents only removal from All bookmarks. Client adds, “The one thing I’d count on is being able to open that archive later to see or bring back what I set aside.” Round 18 maker then presents the Archive view and Restore, which the client accepts.
decisions.note: The client surfaces and requests the missing separate archive view and reversible restore behavior. Round 18 is the linked resolution, not a second opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 19 and 21: maker presents confirmed deletion that removes the bookmark permanently instead of archiving it; client explicitly approves “the right difference from archiving.”
decisions.note: Conforming permanent-delete and archive/delete distinction decision during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 22: maker presents rejecting `not-a-link`, keeping the input open, and requiring a complete web address; client approves saving nothing for an invalid address.
decisions.note: Conforming enforcement of the required-URL constraint during edge-case review.

decisions.evidence: Round 23: maker presents saving a syntactically valid URL even when remote metadata retrieval fails, with an editable address-based fallback title; client approves this failure handling.
decisions.note: This is a conforming failure fallback: metadata collection is attempted, while an unreachable target does not discard a valid URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 24 maker proposes preventing a second copy, reporting that the URL is already saved, and merely highlighting the existing bookmark. Client approves because it “takes me straight to the one I already have,” without mentioning editing it.
decisions.note: Duplicate creation is prevented, but the presented response does not guide the user into editing the existing bookmark as required. The client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 28: maker presents case-insensitive duplicate-tag detection, retaining one `javascript` label; client approves avoiding near-identical tags.
decisions.note: Conforming enforcement of tag-name uniqueness during edge-case review.

decisions.evidence: Round 29: maker states that canceling a delete confirmation leaves the bookmark unchanged; client confirms that this is the expected safety behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming delete-cancellation decision during edge-case review.

decisions.evidence: Round 30: maker presents limiting an unusually long title to two lines while allowing the URL to wrap; client says this keeps the list easy to scan without losing the address.
decisions.note: Conforming readability-first handling of long list-item content.

decisions.evidence: Round 31: maker asks whether a captured title should remain until the user edits it; client explicitly chooses that behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming post-save title persistence and user-controlled editing decision; it does not cure the separate missing pre-save editing divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 32: maker presents rejecting an invalid edited URL, retaining the open edit form, and leaving the saved bookmark unchanged; client approves.
decisions.note: Conforming validation behavior for the URL portion of bookmark editing; it does not cure the separate incomplete edit-field divergence.
